newsitem.title: FRANCE: Preparations for Ariane-5 rocket launch start.
newsitem.headline: Preparations for Ariane-5 rocket launch start.

text.p: Formal preparations for the launch of Western Europe's second Ariane-5 rocket in late September have started in French Guiana, a year after the first Ariane-5 blew up, officials said on Monday.

"Over the next few weeks, mechanical, fluid and electrical integration of the cryogenic main stage, the solid booster stage, the vehicle equipment bay and the upper stage of the launcher will be proceeding in the launcher integration building," the European Space Agency (ESA) and the French Space Agency (CNES) said in a joint statement.
"Meanwhile, various tests, flight program functional simulations in particular will be continuing in Europe," it said.

The first Ariane-5 rocket exploded 37 seconds after launch in June 1996 in a major setback for the ten-year, $9 billion programme. An investigation identified software problems in the rocket's guidance system.

Last year's failure has delayed the rocket's commercial start by over a year. Ariane-5 is designed to keep Europe in the lead in launching heavy satellites well into the next century and eventually lead to a manned European Space programme.
The rocket is prepared and launched from the ESA launch centre in Kourou, French Guiana on northeast coast of South America.
